title: Enterprise Identity & Agent RBAC
tagline: Scoped tool tokens, delegated agent auth, SCIM provisioning and row-level security, so an AI agent can only touch what its human is allowed to touch.
covers: HS256 scoped JWTs for tool calls: audience, expiry, clock skew, alg=none and tamper refusal
Agent-to-human delegation (RFC 8693 style): scopes narrowed, act claim, TTL capped
SCIM 2.0 create / PATCH / deactivate / delete with group-to-role mapping
Row-level security: deny by default, claim-matched rows, column masking
OIDC ID-token claim checks: iss, aud/azp, exp, iat, nonce
gaps: SAML assertion parsing and XML signature checks
RS256/ES256 signatures and JWKS key fetch (HS256 only here)
A real IdP (Okta / Entra) and a real Postgres RLS policy; the logic is the same, the wiring is not

ops.label: Issue tool token
ops.help: Mint a 5-minute token that lets one agent call two CRM tools. Scopes are the allow-list.

ops.label: Verify before tool call
ops.help: The tool server checks the token before it runs. Change required_scope to crm.delete to see a refusal, or move now past expiry.

ops.label: Delegate human to agent
ops.help: Alice's token is exchanged for a narrower agent token. Scopes = requested AND Alice's AND the agent's allow-list. The act claim records the agent.

ops.label: SCIM provisioning
ops.help: The IdP creates a user, adds a group, then deactivates them. Roles are recomputed after each request: a deactivated user has none.

ops.label: Row-level security
ops.help: A finance agent asks for invoices. It sees only its own department's rows, with the IBAN masked.

ops.label: OIDC claim checks
ops.help: Claim checks after the signature passes. This token has a wrong nonce (replay) and two audiences without azp.

why: When an AI agent acts inside a company, the first question from security is: who is it acting for, and what can it touch? This repo answers that with the same building blocks enterprises already use (SSO claims, SCIM, scoped tokens, row-level security), wired so the agent can never hold more access than the human it works for, and so access is removed the moment the IdP deactivates that human.
